maya: Heads up — p95 decode latency jumped ~2.2x on the canary after the scheduler + kv-prefetch merge (commit abc123). CI perf job flagged it: https://ci.internal/reports/2187
ryan: saw the alert, digging into traces now. Is this the same kv-prefetch heuristic change from PR #3345?
kai: yup, that PR changed the prefetch window to be time-since-last-access-based instead of fixed token-window. Intended to reduce memory churn but might be causing more frequent evictions for shortseq workloads.
anna: CI shows the failure on decode-longseq+small-batch workload, interesting — that combo tends to exercise both kernel selector and kv cache hotpaths.
ci-bot: [perf-test] perf/daily/decode-p95: baseline=55ms, canary=125ms, delta=+127% (regression threshold breached)
maya: I grabbed a perf profile from the canary instance. Main hotspots: attention kernel fallback (fast_attn -> safe_attn), frequent kv cache reloads, and scheduler doing a lot of tiny dispatches. snippet:
```
# nvprof-like summary (top kernels)
fast_attn_dispatch            12ms (50 calls)
safe_attn_dispatch            68ms (12 calls)
kv_prefetch_dispatch          45ms (200 calls)
batch_dispatch_overhead       30ms (500 calls)
```
ryan: that matches what i'm seeing — many small batches are hitting the runtime which forces the kernel selector to pick safe_attn due to heuristics that favor contiguous mem paths when seq_len fluctuates. The new prefetch timing causes warmups mid-request.
kai: note: the old code used `if seq_stddev > X: prefer_safe_attn` and we replaced it with `if last_access_delta < T` to decide prefetch, plus we consolidated decision points. I can push a quick diff to reintroduce a debounce on prefetches.
anna: can we reproduce locally with the perf harness? I can run the small-batch/longseq scenario with the merged binary.
maya: yes — run `./perf_harness --workload decode_longseq_smallbatch --repeat 1000 --kv-mode=canary` and capture /tmp/profile.nv. Also enable kernel logging: `export RUNTIME_LOG=kernel_selector:debug`.
ryan: experiment notes: when I disabled prefetch entirely, p95 dropped back to baseline. When I kept prefetch but added a 50ms debounce between prefetches per allocation, p95 improved ~30%. So the prefetch timing is thrashing the KV cache and forcing re-materialization and kernel fallback.
kai: OK i'll prepare a revert PR for the prefetch heuristic and a follow-up to add debounce + a tunable env var for prefetch_window_ms. Do we want a canary hold until revert lands?
maya: yes, put canary on hold. ops — can you hold rollout? @ops (not in thread)
anna: repro run attached: /artifacts/2187654321/repro.log — shows repeated `kv_miss` and `alloc_eviction` entries. snippet: `kv_miss key=prefix:123 attempt=7` repeated.
ci-bot: [action] created issue PERF-3127 referencing commit abc123 and attached perf-report: https://ci.internal/issues/PERF-3127
ryan: for post-mortem, we should add a regression test that simulates short bursts of small batches with interleaved long sequences. Also add an assertion in kernel selector that avoids rapid flip-flopping between fast_attn and safe_attn in the same request.
kai: pushed draft revert: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/commit/revert-abc123, running unit + perf smoke now. If green i'll request a rollback.
maya: thanks. once revert is in, let's run the nightly perf hinge tests and then iterate on the debounce approach in a smaller follow-up PR. Keep notifications in this thread. :thumbsup:
